37:1: Interpretation of Surat As-Saffat It is Meccan Al-Nasa’i said: Ismail bin Mas’ud told us, Khalid - meaning Ibn Al-Harith - told us, on the authority of Ibn Abi Dhi’b, who said: Al-Harith bin Abd Al-Rahman told us, on the authority of Salim bin Abdullah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Umar, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to command us to make the recitation brief and to say Amen to Al-Saffat. Al-Nasa’i is the only one who transmitted this. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of al-A’mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Abdullah ibn Mas’ud, may God be pleased with him, that he said: And those who rank up in rows meaning the angels. And those who drive away meaning the angels. And those who recite the Reminder meaning the angels. This is what Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said, as did Masruq, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, Mujahid, al-Suddi, Qatadah, and al-Rabi’ ibn Anas. Qatadah said: The angels are in rows in the heaven. Muslim said: Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah told us: Muhammad ibn Fadil told us, on the authority of Abu Malik al-Ashja’i, on the authority of Rib’i, on the authority of Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “We have been given precedence over people in three things: Our rows have been made like the rows of the angels, the entire earth has been made a place of prostration for us, and its soil has been made a means of purification for us if we cannot find water.” Muslim, Abu Dawud, al-Nasa’i, and Ibn Majah also narrated from the hadith of al-A’mash, on the authority of al-Musayyab ibn Rafi’, on the authority of Tamim ibn Tarfa, on the authority of Jabir ibn Samurah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Why do you not line up as the angels line up before their Lord? We said: How do the angels line up before their Lord? The Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) said: They complete the front rows and stand close together in the row. As-Suddi and others said that the meaning of the words of God, Those who drive away with a driving force is that they drive away the clouds. Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas said: Those who drive away with a driving force is what God, the Most High, forbade in the Quran. Malik narrated the same from Zayd ibn Aslam: Those who recite the Reminder As-Suddi said: The angels bring the Book and the Quran from God to the people. This verse is like the words of God, the Most High: Those who cast down the Reminder, as an excuse or a warning. And the words of God, the Most High: Indeed, your God is One, Lord of the heavens and the earth This is what is sworn by, that He, the Most High, is there is no god but Him, Lord of the heavens and the earth “and what is between them” meaning of the creation and Lord of the Easts meaning He is the Owner who controls creation by subjecting it to what is in it of fixed and moving planets that appear in the east and set in the west. He was satisfied with mentioning the Easts instead of the Wests because they indicate Him. He made this clear in His Almighty’s saying: So I swear by the Lord of the Easts and the Wests, that We are indeed Able. And He, the Almighty, said in another verse: Lord of the two Easts and Lord of the two Wests, meaning in the winter and summer for the sun and the moon.

37:6: The Almighty informs us that He has adorned the lowest heaven for those on earth who look at it with the adornment of the planets. It has been read with the addition and with the substitute, and both have the same meaning. The light of the planets and the fixed ones pierces the transparent body of the heaven, illuminating it for the people on earth, as the Almighty said: And We have certainly adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and made them missiles against the devils, and We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze. And the Almighty said: “And We have certainly placed within the heaven constellations and have adorned it for the observers. And We have protected it from every outcast devil, except for one who steals a hearing, and a clear flame pursues him.” So His Almighty saying here: And as a safeguard means, And We have protected it as a safeguard, “from every rebellious devil,” meaning the rebellious, violent one. If he wants to steal a hearing, a piercing flame will come to him and burn him. For this reason, the Almighty said, They do not listen to the highest assembly, meaning so that they do not reach the highest assembly, which is the heavens and the angels in them, when they speak what God Almighty inspires of what He says of His law and power. This was also explained in the hadiths that we mentioned when God the Most High said: Until, when fear has departed from their hearts, they say, ‘What has your Lord said?’ They say, ‘The truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand.’ For this reason God the Most High said: And they are pelted meaning they are pelted from every side meaning from every direction, aiming towards the sky from it, repelled meaning pelted with stones by which they are repelled, rebuked and prevented from reaching that and they are pelted and for them is a lasting punishment meaning in the Hereafter they will have a permanent, painful, and continuous punishment as God the Most High said: And We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze. And God the Most High said: Except for he who snatches a snatch meaning except for he who snatches from the devils a snatch, which is a word that he hears from the sky and throws it to the one below him and the other throws it to the one below him. Perhaps the meteor will overtake him before he utters it, and perhaps he will utter it by the decree of God the Most High before the meteor comes to him and burns him, so the other will take it to the soothsayer as mentioned in the hadith. For this reason He said: Except for he who snatches a snatch and is pursued by a piercing flame meaning an illuminating one. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The devils had stations in the heavens. He said: They would listen to the revelation. He said: The stars did not move, and the devils were not shot. He said: When they heard the revelation, they would come down to earth and add nine words. He said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, whenever the devil intended to sit, a meteor would come to him and would not miss him until it burned him. He said: They complained about that to Satan, may God curse him, and he said: It is nothing but a recent matter. He sent his soldiers and thereupon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was standing praying between two mountains of Nakhl. Waki’ meant the valley of Nakhl. He said: They returned to Satan and informed him, and he said: This is what had happened. And the hadiths that were reported with the reports in this meaning will come, God willing, when God Almighty says, informing us about the jinn, that they said: “And we touched the heaven but found it filled with stern guards and flaming fires. And we used to sit therein in stations to listen. But whoever listens now will find a flaming fire lying in wait for him. And we do not know.” Is it evil that I intend for those on earth, or does their Lord intend for them a right course?

And we do not know.” Is it evil that I intend for those on earth, or does their Lord intend for them a right course?
37:10: God Almighty informs us that He has adorned the lowest heaven for those who look at it from among the people of the earth with the adornment of the planets. It has been read with the addition and with the substitute, and both have the same meaning. The light of the planets and the fixed ones pierces the transparent body of the heaven, so they shine for the people of the earth, as God Almighty said: And We have certainly adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and made them missiles against the devils and have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze. And He Almighty said: “And We have certainly placed within the heaven constellations and have adorned it for the observers. And We have protected it from every outcast devil, except for one who steals a hearing, and a clear flame pursues him.” So His Almighty saying here: And as a safeguard means and We have protected it as a safeguard from every rebellious devil, meaning the rebellious, violent one. If he wants to steal a hearing, a piercing flame will come to him and burn him. For this reason, God Almighty said: They do not listen to the highest assembly, meaning so that they do not reach the highest assembly, which is the heavens and the angels in them, if they speak what God Almighty inspires of what He says it from His law and power, as was explained previously in the hadiths that we mentioned when God the Most High said: Until, when fear has departed from their hearts, they say, ‘What has your Lord said?’ They say, ‘The truth, and He is the Most High, the Grand.’ For this reason, God the Most High said: And they are pelted meaning they are pelted from every side meaning from every direction, aiming towards the sky, repelled meaning pelted with stones by which they are repelled, rebuked, and prevented from reaching that, and they are pelted. And for them is a lasting punishment meaning in the Hereafter, they will have a permanent, painful, and continuous punishment, as He the Most High said: And We have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze. And God the Most High said: Except for he who snatches a snatch meaning except for he who snatches from the devils a snatch, which is a word that he hears from the sky and throws it to the one below him, and the other throws it to the one below him. Perhaps the meteor will overtake him before he utters it, and perhaps he will utter it by the decree of God the Most High before the meteor comes to him and burns him, and the other will take it to the soothsayer, as was mentioned previously in the hadith. For this reason, He said: Except for he who snatches a snatch, and a piercing flame pursues him. Any enlightened one. Ibn Jarir said: Abu Kurayb told us: Waki’ told us, on the authority of Israel, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The devils had stations in the heavens. He said: They would listen to the revelation. He said: The stars did not move and the devils were not shot. He said: When they heard the revelation, they would come down to earth and add nine words. He said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was sent, whenever the devil intended to sit, a meteor would come to him and would not miss him until it burned him. He said: They complained about that to Satan, may God curse him, and he said: It is nothing but a recent matter. He sent his soldiers and thereupon the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was standing praying between two mountains of Nakhl. Waki’ meant the valley of Nakhl. He said: They returned to Satan and informed him, and he said: This is what had happened. And we used to sit therein in stations to listen. But whoever listens now will find a flaming fire lying in wait for him. And we do not know.” Is it evil that I intend for those on earth, or does their Lord intend for them a right course?
37:11: God Almighty says: Ask these deniers of the Resurrection, which is more difficult in creation - they, or the heavens and the earth and what is between them of angels and devils and great creatures? Ibn Masoud, may God be pleased with him, read, Or of Our number, for they acknowledge that these creatures are more difficult in creation than them. If this is the case, then why do they deny the Resurrection? And they see something greater than what they denied, as the Almighty said: The creation of the heavens and the earth is greater than the creation of mankind, but most people do not know. Then He explained that they were created from something weak, saying: Indeed, We created them from sticky clay. Mujahid, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, and Ad-Dahhak said: It is the good part that sticks together. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them, and Ikrimah said: It is the sticky good. Qatadah said: It is what sticks to the hand. And the Almighty said: Rather, I am amazed, and they ridicule. That is, O Muhammad, I am amazed at the denial of these deniers of the Resurrection, and you are certain and believe in what God Almighty has informed us about the amazing matter, which is the return of bodies after their destruction, and they are against your command due to the intensity of their denial, and they ridicule what you say to them about that. Qatada said: Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) was amazed and ridiculed the misguidance of the children of Adam. And when they see a sign, meaning a clear proof of that, they scoff. Mujahid and Qatada said they mock. And they say, ‘This is nothing but obvious magic.’ That is, what you have brought is nothing but obvious magic. When we have died and become dust and bones, will we indeed be resurrected? * Or our forefathers of old? They find that unlikely and deny it. Say, ‘Yes, and you will be humbled.’ That is, say to them, O Muhammad, “Yes, you will be resurrected on the Day of Resurrection after you have become dust and bones, humbled, meaning insignificant before the mighty power, as God, the Most High, said: “And all will come to Him humbled.” Then He, the Most High, said: It will be only one blast, and at once they will be looking on. That is, it will be only one command from God, the Almighty, calling them with one call to emerge from the earth, and at once they will be before Him, looking at the horrors of the Day of Resurrection. And God knows best.

37:20: God the Almighty tells us about what the unbelievers will say on the Day of Resurrection, that they will blame themselves and admit that they were unjust to themselves in this world. Then, when they witness the horrors of the Resurrection, they will feel deep regret, as regret will not benefit them. And they will say, ‘Woe to us! This is the Day of Judgment.’ The angels and believers will say, This is the Day of Judgment, which you used to deny. This is said to them as a rebuke and rebuke. God the Almighty commands the angels to distinguish the unbelievers from the believers in the place of their gathering and resurrection. For this reason, God the Almighty said, Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses. An-Nu’man ibn Bashir may God be pleased with him said that by their spouses he means those who are similar to them and their equals. Ibn Abbas, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, Mujahid, As-Suddi, Abu Salih, Abu Al-Aaliyah, and Zayd ibn Aslam said the same. Sufyan Ath-Thawri said, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of An-Nu’man ibn Bashir, on the authority of Umar ibn Al-Khattab may God be pleased with him: Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses, meaning their brothers. Sharik narrated from Samak from An-Nu'man who said: I heard Umar say: Gather together those who did wrong and their spouses. He said: Those who look like them. He said: The adulterers will come with the adulterers, the usurers with the usurers, and the wine drinkers with the wine drinkers. Khasif narrated from Muqsim from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both: Their spouses will be their women. This is strange, but the first is known, as narrated by Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr from him: Their spouses will be their companions, and what they used to worship besides God, i.e., idols and rivals, will be gathered with them in their places. God the Almighty said: Then guide them to the path to Hellfire. This is like His saying: "And We will gather them on the Day of Resurrection on their faces, blind, dumb and deaf. Their refuge will be Hell. Whenever it subsides, We will increase their blazing fire." God the Almighty said: Stop them, for they will be questioned. This means stop them until they are asked about their deeds and words that they uttered in this world, as Ad-Dahhak said from Ibn Abbas, meaning: Detain them, for they will be held accountable. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Al-Nufaili told us, Al-Mu'tamir bin Sulaiman told us, he said: I heard Laith narrating on the authority of Bashir, on the authority of Anas bin Malik may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Whoever calls to something, it will be stopped with him until the Day of Resurrection, never leaving it or departing from it, even if a man calls a man. Then he recited: Stop them, for indeed, they will be questioned. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Laith bin Abi Sulaym. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ya’qub bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Mu’tamir, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of a man, on the authority of Anas may God be pleased with him, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him). Abdullah bin Al-Mubarak said: I heard Uthman bin Za’idah say: The first thing a man will be asked about will be his companions, then it will be said to them by way of rebuke and rebuke: Why do you not support one another? That is, as you claimed, you are a group of victors. Rather, today they are submissive, that is, they submit to the command of God, neither disobeying Him nor deviating from it. And God knows best.

37:27: God Almighty mentions that the disbelievers will blame one another on the Day of Resurrection just as they will quarrel in the depths of Hellfire. “Then the weak will say to those who were arrogant, ‘Indeed, we were your followers, so can you relieve us of a share of the Fire?’ Those who were arrogant will say, ‘Indeed, we are all in it. Indeed, God has judged between the servants.’” God Almighty also says, “And if you could but see when the wrongdoers are made to stand before their Lord, returning their words to one another. Those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, ‘If it had not been for you, we would have been believers.’ Those who were arrogant will say to those who were oppressed, ‘Did we avert you from guidance after it had come to you? Rather, you were criminals.’ And those who were oppressed will say to those who were arrogant, ‘Rather, it was [your] plotting by night and by day when you ordered us to disbelieve in God and attribute to Him equals.’ And they will conceal their regret when they see the punishment, and We have put shackles on the necks of those who disbelieved. Are they recompensed except for what they used to do?” And thus they will say to them here, Indeed, you used to come to Us from the right. He said, Ad-Dahhak narrated from Ibn Abbas, they say: You used to subjugate us with your power over us because we were humiliated and you were honored. Mujahid said: It means from the truth, while the disbelievers say it to the devils. Qatadah said: The humans said to the jinn: You used to come to us from the right, meaning from the direction of good, forbidding us from it and delaying us from it. As-Suddi said: You come to us from the direction of truth, beautifying falsehood for us and turning us away from the truth. Al-Hasan said about the verse: Indeed, you used to come to us from the right, meaning: God comes to him at every good he wants and turns him away from it. Ibn Zayd said: It means: You stand between us and good and turn us back from Islam, faith and doing the good that we have been commanded to do. Yazid said: Polytheism from the direction of there is no god but God, and Khasif said: They mean from their right side. Ikrimah said: Indeed, you used to come to us from the right, meaning from where we feel safe. And the Almighty said: They said, ‘Rather, you were not believers.’ The leaders from among the jinn and mankind said to the followers, “The matter is not as you claim. Rather, your hearts were denying faith and were prone to disbelief and disobedience. “And we had no authority over you.” That is, no proof of the truth of what we called you to. Rather, you were a transgressing people. That is, there was transgression and transgression among you, and that is why you responded to us and abandoned the truth that the prophets brought you and presented to you proofs for the truth of what they brought you, but you opposed it. “So the word of our Lord came into effect upon us, ‘Indeed, we are to taste it.’ So we led you astray. Indeed, we were going astray.” The leaders said to the weak, the word of God came into effect upon us, I am among the wretched ones who will taste the punishment on the Day of Resurrection. “So we led you astray.” That is, we called you to misguidance. Indeed, we were going astray. That is, we called you to what we are in, and you responded to us. God, the Blessed and Exalted, said: So indeed, on that Day, they will be partners in the punishment. That is, everyone will be in the Fire, each according to his ability. “Thus will We deal with the criminals. Indeed, They were, that is, in this world, “when it was said to them, ‘There is no god but God,’ they were arrogant,” meaning they were too arrogant to say it as the believers say it. Ibn Abi Hatim said, ‘Ubayd God ibn Akhi ibn Wahb told us, my uncle told us, Al-Layth told us, on the authority of Ibn Musafir, meaning Abd al-Rahman ibn Khalid, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Sa’id ibn al-Musayyab, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I have been commanded to fight the people until they say, ‘There is no god but God.’ So whoever says, ‘There is no god but God,’ his wealth and his life are protected from me, except for what is due, and his reckoning is with God Almighty.” And God Almighty revealed in His Noble Book and mentioned a people who were arrogant, saying, Indeed, when it was said to them, ‘There is no god but God,’ they were arrogant. Ibn Abi Hatim also said, my father told us, Abu Salamah Musa ibn Ismail told us, Hammad told us, on the authority of Sa’id al-Jariri, on the authority of Abu al-Ala’, who said: The Jews will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and it will be said to them, ‘What did you worship?’ They will say, We worship God and Ezra. It will be said to them, Take the one on the left. Then the Christians will be brought and it will be said to them, What did you worship? They will say, We worship God and the Messiah. It will be said to them, Take the one on the left. Then the polytheists will be brought and it will be said to them, There is no god but God, and they will be arrogant. Then...Take the one on the left.” Abu Nadrah said, They will fly faster than birds. Abu Al-Ala’ said, Then the Muslims will be brought and it will be said to them, “What did you worship? They will say, We used to worship God. It will be said to them, Would you recognize Him when you saw Him? They will say, Yes. It will be said to them, How can you recognize Him when you have not seen Him? They will say, We know that there is no equal to Him. He said, So He, the Blessed and Exalted, recognizes them and saves the believers, and God, the Exalted, saves them. “And they say, ‘Shall we indeed abandon our gods for the sake of a mad poet?’” That is, shall we abandon the worship of our gods and the gods of our fathers because of the words of this mad poet, meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace? God, the Most High, said, in refutation of them and in response to them, Rather, he has brought the truth, meaning the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, brought the truth in all of God’s law for him of report and requests. And he confirmed the messengers, that is, he confirmed them in what they reported about him of praiseworthy attributes and sound methods, and he reported about God, the Most High, in His law and command, as they reported. Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you, the verse.

That is why He the Almighty said here: Except the chosen servants of God, meaning they will not taste the painful punishment, nor will they be questioned in the reckoning. Rather, their bad deeds will be overlooked if they have any bad deeds, and they will be rewarded for a good deed tenfold, up to seven hundredfold, or many times over, up to whatever multiplication God the Almighty wills. And the saying of the Most High: For those is a known provision. Qatada and As-Suddi said: It means Paradise. Then he explained it with the saying of the Most High: Fruits, meaning varied. And they will be honored, meaning they will be served, entertained, and blessed. In the Gardens of Delight, on thrones facing each other. Mujahid said: They will not look at each other’s backs. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya ibn Abdak Al-Qazwini told us: Hassan ibn Hassan told us: Ibrahim ibn Bishr told us: Yahya ibn Ma’in told us: Ibrahim Al-Qurashi told us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Shurahbil, on the authority of Zayd ibn Abi Awfa, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came out to us and recited this verse: On thrones facing each other, looking at each other. This is a strange hadith. God the Almighty said: And there will be circulated among them a cup from a flowing stream, white, a delight to the drinkers, therein no headache, nor will they get drunk from it. Just as God the Almighty said in another verse: And there will be circulated among them immortal youths, with goblets and pitchers and a cup from a flowing stream, therefrom they will not get a headache, nor will they get drunk from it. God the Almighty has cleared the wine of Paradise of the afflictions that are found in the wine of this world, such as headaches and stomach pain, which is the headache, and its loss of reason in general. So God the Almighty said here: And there will be circulated among them a cup from a flowing stream, meaning wine from flowing rivers, and they will not fear its interruption or its emptiness. Malik said, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam: “A white flowing wine means its color is bright, beautiful, and radiant, unlike the wine of this world in its ugly, bad appearance, such as redness, blackness, yellowness, or cloudiness, etc., which repels a sound nature.” And the Almighty’s saying: A delight to those who drink means its taste is as pleasant as its colour, and the pleasant taste is evidence of the pleasant smell, unlike the wine of this world in all of that. And the Almighty’s saying: Therein is no ghast means it does not have a ghastly effect, which is a stomach ache, as said by Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, Mujahid, Qatadah and Ibn Zayd, just as the wine of this world does with colic and the like due to its high water content. And it was said that what is meant by ghast here is a headache, and it was narrated thus from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Qatadah said it is a headache and a stomach ache, and from him and from al-Suddi it is: Their minds are not taken away, as the poet said: The cup still kills us and takes the first place Sa`id ibn Jubayr said: There is no harm or objection to it, and the correct statement of Mujahid is that it is a stomach ache. God the Almighty said: nor will they be intoxicated by it Mujahid said: Their minds will not be lost. This is what Ibn Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka`b, al-Hasan, Ata’ ibn Abi Muslim al-Khurasani, al-Suddi and others said. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: There are four characteristics of wine: intoxication, headache, vomiting and urination. God the Almighty mentioned the wine of Paradise and purified it from these characteristics as He mentioned in Surat as-Saffat. God the Almighty said: And with them will be chaste women meaning chaste women who do not look at anyone but their husbands. This is what Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with him and his father said, as did Mujahid, Zayd ibn Aslam, Qatadah, al-Suddi and others. And His saying, the Blessed and Most High: eye meaning beautiful eyes. It was said that they had large eyes, and it goes back to the first, which are the big-eyed ones. So He described their eyes with beauty and chastity, like the saying of Zulaykha about Joseph, peace be upon him, when she brought him out to those women, and they magnified and glorified him and thought he was an angel from the angels because of his beauty and the splendor of his appearance. She said: “This is he for whom you blamed me. And I did indeed try to seduce him, but he refused.” That is, despite this beauty, he is chaste, pious, and pure. And thus are the wide-eyed houris good and beautiful. For this reason, the Almighty said: And with them will be maidens restricting their glances and [whose eyes are] narrow-eyed. And His saying, the Most High: As if they were white, hidden, He described them with the delicacy of bodies in the best colors. Ali bin Abi Talha said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, As if they were white, hidden, meaning the hidden pearls. And here he recites the verse of Abu Dahbal, the poet, which is his saying in a poem of his: She is a flower like a pearl of the sea, distinguished from a hidden essence Al-Hasan said: As if they were hidden eggs, meaning protected and untouched by hands. Al-Suddi said: The eggs are hidden in their nests. Saeed bin Jubair said: As if they were hidden eggs, meaning the inside of the egg. Ata’ Al-Khurasani said: It is the mesocarp that is between the upper shell and the egg’s core. Al-Suddi said: As if they were hidden eggs, meaning the white of the egg when its shell is removed. Ibn Jarir chose it because he said: hidden. He said: The upper shell is touched by the wing of the bird and the nest and the hands reach it, unlike its inside, and God knows best. Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Wahb told us: Muhammad ibn al-Faraj al-Sadfi al-Dimyati told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Hashim, on the authority of Ibn Abi Karima, on the authority of Hisham, on the authority of al-Hasan, on the authority of his mother, on the authority of Umm Salamah, may God be pleased with her, who said: I said: O Messenger of God, tell me about the statement of God Almighty: Houris with wide, beautiful eyes. He said: The large eyes, the lips of the houri are like the wings of an eagle. I said: O Messenger of God, tell me about the statement of God Almighty: As if they were hidden eggs. He said: Their thinness is like the thinness of the skin whose head is inside the egg that is next to the shell, which is the gharqa’. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abu Ghassan Al-Nahdi told us, Abd Al-Salam bin Harb told us, on the authority of Laith, on the authority of Al-Rabi’ bin Anas, on the authority of Anas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I am the first of the people to emerge when they are sent, and I am their orator when they arrive, and I am their bringer of good tidings when they grieve, and I am their intercessor when they are imprisoned. The banner of praise on that Day will be in my hand, and I am the most honored of the children of Adam in the sight of God Almighty, and I am not boasting. A thousand servants will circulate around me like hidden eggs - or hidden pearls.” And God Almighty knows best.
37:50: God the Almighty tells us about the people of Paradise that some of them will turn to others, asking about their conditions and how they were in this world and what they suffered in it, and that is from their conversation over their drinks, their gathering to drink and their company in their gatherings while they sit on couches and the servants are before them, striving and bringing every great good of food, drink, clothing and other things that no eye has seen, no ear has heard and no human heart has conceived. One of them will say, ‘Indeed I had a companion.’ Mujahid said, meaning a devil. Al-Awfi said, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, that he is a polytheist who has a companion from among the people of faith in this world. There is no contradiction between the words of Mujahid and Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, for the devil may be from the jinn and whispers in the soul, and he may be from humans and say words that the ears hear, and both of them cooperate. God the Almighty said, They inspire to one another decorative speech in delusion. And each of them whispers, as God the Almighty said, From the evil of the retreating whisperer * Who whispers in the breasts of mankind * From among the jinn and mankind. And for this reason, a speaker said Among them is, “I had a companion who said, ‘Are you indeed among the believers?’ That is, do you believe in the resurrection, the rising, the reckoning, and the reward? He says that in a way that expresses amazement, denial, rejection, disbelief, and stubbornness. When we have died and become dust and bones, will we then be recompensed? Mujahid and As-Suddi said, We will be held accountable. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Muhammad ibn Ka’b Al-Qurazi said, We will be rewarded for our deeds. Both are correct. God, the Most High, said, He said, ‘Are you looking forward?’ That is, the believer will say to his companions and those sitting with him from among the people of Paradise. So he looked and saw him in the midst of Hellfire. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, Sa’id ibn Jubayr, Khalid Al-Asri, Qatadah, As-Suddi, and Ata’ Al-Khurasani said, It means in the middle of Hellfire. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said, In the middle of Hellfire, like a blazing meteor. Qatadah said, It was mentioned to us that he looked and saw the skulls of the people boiling. It was mentioned to us that Ka’b Al-Ahbar said, “In Paradise there are windows. If one of its people wants to look at his enemy in the Fire, he looks into them and his gratitude increases.” He said, ‘By God, you were almost thrown down.’ The believer says, addressing the disbeliever, By God, you were almost thrown down. “And were it not for the grace of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth.” That is, were it not for the grace of God upon me, I would have been like you in the midst of Hell, where you are brought forth with you in torment. But He was gracious to me and had mercy upon me, so He guided me to faith and directed me to His Oneness. And we would not have been guided had God not guided us. And the Almighty’s saying: Then are we not to die * Except for our first death? And are we not to be punished? This is from the words of the believer, envying himself for what God has given him of eternity in Paradise and residence in the abode of honor without death or punishment therein. For this reason, the Almighty said: Indeed, this is the great attainment. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Abdullah Al-Dhahrani told us, Hafs bin Omar Al-Adani told us, Al-Hakam bin Abaan told us, on the authority of Ikrimah, who said: Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said regarding the words of God, the Blessed and Exalted, to the people of Paradise: Eat and drink at ease for what you used to do. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: The Almighty’s saying: at ease means they will not die therein. Then they will say: Then are we not to die * Except for our first death? Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: They knew that every pleasure is cut short by death, so they said: Then are we not to die * Except for our first death, and we are not to be punished? It was said: No, indeed this is the great attainment. And His, the Most High, saying: For the like of this let the workers work. Qatada said: This is from the words of the people of Paradise. Ibn Jarir said: It is from the words of God Almighty, and its meaning is for the like of this pleasure and this attainment, so let the workers work in this world to reach it in the Hereafter. They mentioned the story of two men who were partners among the Children of Israel, which falls within the generality of this noble verse. Abu Ja`far bin Jarir said: Ishaq bin Ibrahim bin Habib bin Al-Shahid told us: `Atab bin Bashir told us, on the authority of Khasif, on the authority of Furat bin Tha`laba Al-Nahrani, regarding His statement: Indeed, I had a companion, he said: Two men were partners, and eight thousand dinars were collected for them. One of them had a trade and the other did not. The one who had a trade said to the other: “You do not have a trade. I see myself only leaving you and sharing it with you.” So he shared it with him and left him. Then the man bought a house. For a thousand dinars, it belonged to a king who died. So he called his companion and showed him the house. He said, How do you see this house? I bought it for a thousand dinars. He said, How beautiful it is. So when he left, he said, O God, my companion bought this house for a thousand dinars, and I ask You for a house from the houses of Paradise, so give a thousand dinars in charity. Then he stayed as long as God willed it to stay. Then he married a woman for a thousand dinars, so God invited him and made him food. When he came to him, he said, I married this woman for a thousand dinars. He said, How beautiful this is. So when he left, he said, O Lord, my companion married a woman for a thousand dinars, and I ask You for a woman from the houris, so give a thousand dinars in charity. Then he stayed as long as God willed it to stay. Then he bought two gardens for two thousand dinars, then he called him and showed him the house. He said, I bought these two gardens for two thousand dinars. He said, How beautiful this is. So when he left, he said, O Lord, my companion bought two gardens for two thousand dinars, and I ask You for two gardens in Paradise, so give a thousand dinars in charity. Then the king came to them and took them both. Then he went with this charitable person and brought him into a house that pleased him, and suddenly a woman appeared. He illuminated what was beneath it of its beauty. Then he entered two gardens and a thing of which God is Knowing. Then he said, How similar this is to a man whose affair was such and such. He said, Then you will have this house, the two gardens, and the woman. He said, Then I had a companion who said, ‘Are you indeed among those who believe?’ It was said to him, Then he is in Hellfire. He said, Are you seeing? So he looked and saw him in the depths of Hellfire. Then he said, “By God, you were almost sent back. And were it not for the grace of my Lord, I would have been among those brought forth.” The verses Ibn Jarir said, This strengthens the reading of the one who read, ‘Are you indeed among those who believe?’ with the shaddah. Ibn Abi Hatim said, “Al-Hasan ibn Arafa told us, ‘Amr ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Abar told us, Abu Hafs told us, “I asked Ismail al-Suddi about this verse, ‘One of them said, ‘Indeed, I had a companion * who said, ‘Are you indeed among those who believe?’” He said, He said to me, ‘What reminded you of this?’ I said, I read it just now and wanted to ask you about it. He said, “But remember. There were two partners among the Children of Israel, one of them a believer and the other a disbeliever. They parted for six thousand dinars, each of them three thousand dinars. Then they parted.” So they stayed as long as God willed them to stay, then they met and the unbeliever said to the believer, What did you do with your money? Did you spend it on something or trade in something? The believer said, “No. So what did you do?” He said, I bought land, palm trees, fruits, and rivers for a thousand dinars. The believer said, Or did you? He said, Yes. The believer went back and when it was night he prayed as long as God willed him to pray. When he finished, he took a thousand dinars and placed them in front of him and said, O God, so-and-so - meaning his unbeliever partner - bought land, palm trees, fruits, and rivers for a thousand dinars, then he will die tomorrow and leave them. O God, I have bought from You with these thousand dinars land, palm trees, fruits, and rivers in Paradise.” He said, Then he came in the morning and distributed them among the poor. Then they stayed as long as God willed them to stay, then they met and the unbeliever said to the believer, What did you do with your money? Did you spend it on something? Traded it? He said, No. He said, Then what did you do? He said, My estate was becoming too difficult for me, so I bought… A slave for a thousand dinars, so that they may take care of it and work for me in it. The believer said to him, Did you do it? He said, Yes. So the believer returned, and when it was night, he prayed as much as God willed him to pray. When he finished, he took a thousand dinars and placed them in front of him. Then he said, O God, so-and-so - meaning his disbelieving partner - bought a slave from the slaves of this world for a thousand dinars. He will die tomorrow and leave them alone, or they will die and leave him alone. O God, I have bought from You with these thousand dinars a slave in Paradise.” He said, Then he came in the morning and distributed them among the poor. He said, “Then they stayed as long as God willed them to stay, then they met. The disbeliever said to the believer, “What did you do with your wealth? Used it for something or traded with it?” He said, “No. So what did you do?” He said, “My whole affair was settled except one thing: So-and-so’s husband died, so I gave her a thousand dinars as a dowry, and she brought them to me and the same amount with her.” So the believer said to him, Did you do it? He said, Yes. So the believer returned, and when it was night, he prayed as much as God willed him to pray. When he finished, he took the remaining thousand dinars and placed them in front of him and said, O God, so-and-so Meaning his disbelieving partner - he married a woman from the wives of this world for a thousand dinars, then he died tomorrow and left her or she died tomorrow and left him, O God, I propose to You for these thousand dinars a beautiful, beautiful woman in Paradise - he said - then he got up in the morning and divided it among the poor - he said - so the believer was left with nothing. He said: So he put on a shirt of cotton and a woolen cloak, then he took myrrh and put it around his neck, doing things and digging things with his strength. He said: Then a man came to him and said to him: O servant of God, will you hire yourself to me for a month, month after month, to look after my animals, feed them and sweep their waste? He said: I will. He said: So he hired himself to me for a month, month after month, to look after his animals. He said: The owner of the animals would go out every day to look at his animals, and if he saw a lean one among them, he would take hold of its head and slap its neck, then he would say to it: I stole barley last night. He said: When the believer saw this hardship, he said: Let my disbelieving partner come and I will work in his land, so he can feed me this piece of bread day after day and clothe me with these two garments. If they are worn out, he said, so he went after him. He reached his door and saw a palace built high in the sky. And around it were the doormen. He said to them, Ask permission for me to see the owner of this palace, for if you do that, he will be pleased. They said to him, “Go, if you are truthful, and sleep in a corner. When morning comes, approach him.” He said, “So the believer went and threw half of his cloak under him and half over him, then he slept. When morning came, he went to his partner and approached him. His unbelieving partner came out riding. When he saw him, he recognized him, stood up and greeted him and shook hands with him. Then he said to him, “Didn’t you take the money as I took it?” He said, Yes. He said, This is my situation and this is your situation. He said, Yes. He said, Tell me what you did with your money. He said, Do not ask me about it. He said, So what brought you? He said, I came to work in this land of yours and you feed me this piece of bread day after day and clothe me with these two garments when they are worn out. He said, No, but I will do with you what is better than this, but you will not see any good from me until you tell me what you did with your money. He said, I lent it to you. He said, Who? He said, The wealthy and faithful. He said, Who? He said, God is my Lord. He said, while shaking hands with him. Then he pulled his hand away from his hand and He said, Are you indeed among those who believe? When we die and become dust and bones, will we indeed be held accountable? Al-Suddi said, We will be held accountable. He said, Then the unbeliever went off and left him. He said, "When the believer saw him and did not look back, he returned and left him. The believer lives in hardship during a time and the unbeliever lives in ease." He said, "So when the Day of Resurrection comes and God admits the believer into Paradise, he passes by and sees land, palm trees, fruits, and rivers. He says, 'To whom does this belong?' It is said, 'This belongs to you.' He says, 'Glory be to God, or has the bounty of my deeds reached such a degree that I should be rewarded with the like of this?'" He said, "Then he passes by and sees slaves whose number cannot be counted. He says, 'To whom does this belong?' It is said, 'These belong to you.' He says, 'Glory be to God, or has the bounty of my deeds reached such a degree that I should be rewarded with the like of this.'" He said, "Then he passes by and sees a dome of red ruby, hollowed out in it, with a beautiful, beautiful woman in her eyes. He says, 'To whom does this belong?' It is said, 'This belongs to you.' He says, 'Glory be to God, or has the bounty of my deeds reached such a degree that I should be rewarded with the like of this.'" He said, "Then the believer remembers his unbelieving partner and says, 'Indeed, I had a companion.' He says, 'Would you To those who believe, When we die and become dust and bones, shall we then be recompensed? He said, Paradise is high and Hell is deep. Then God Almighty will show him his partner in the middle of Hell from among the people of Hell. When the believer sees him, he will recognize him and say, “By God, you were almost sent back. And had it not been for the grace of my Lord, you would have been among those brought forth. So are we not to die? Except our first death, and we are not to be punished. Indeed, this is the great attainment. For such things let the workers work.” He said: The believer remembers the hardships he went through in this world, and he does not remember anything that was more difficult for him than death.

When he finished, he took the remaining thousand dinars and placed them in front of him and said, O God, so-and-so Meaning his disbelieving partner - he married a woman from the wives of this world for a thousand dinars, then he died tomorrow and left her or she died tomorrow and left him, O God, I propose to You for these thousand dinars a beautiful, beautiful woman in Paradise - he said - then he got up in the morning and divided it among the poor - he said - so the believer was left with nothing. He said: So he put on a shirt of cotton and a woolen cloak, then he took myrrh and put it around his neck, doing things and digging things with his strength. He said: Then a man came to him and said to him: O servant of God, will you hire yourself to me for a month, month after month, to look after my animals, feed them and sweep their waste? He said: I will. He said: So he hired himself to me for a month, month after month, to look after his animals. He said: The owner of the animals would go out every day to look at his animals, and if he saw a lean one among them, he would take hold of its head and slap its neck, then he would say to it: I stole barley last night. He said: When the believer saw this hardship, he said: Let my disbelieving partner come and I will work in his land, so he can feed me this piece of bread day after day and clothe me with these two garments. If they are worn out, he said, so he went after him. He reached his door and saw a palace built high in the sky. And around it were the doormen. He said to them, Ask permission for me to see the owner of this palace, for if you do that, he will be pleased. They said to him, “Go, if you are truthful, and sleep in a corner. When morning comes, approach him.” He said, “So the believer went and threw half of his cloak under him and half over him, then he slept. When morning came, he went to his partner and approached him. His unbelieving partner came out riding. When he saw him, he recognized him, stood up and greeted him and shook hands with him. Then he said to him, “Didn’t you take the money as I took it?” He said, Yes. He said, This is my situation and this is your situation. He said, Yes. He said, Tell me what you did with your money. He said, Do not ask me about it. He said, So what brought you? He said, I came to work in this land of yours and you feed me this piece of bread day after day and clothe me with these two garments when they are worn out. He said, No, but I will do with you what is better than this, but you will not see any good from me until you tell me what you did with your money. He said, I lent it to you. He said, Who? He said, The wealthy and faithful. He said, Who? He said, God is my Lord. He said, while shaking hands with him. Then he pulled his hand away from his hand and He said, Are you indeed among those who believe? When we die and become dust and bones, will we indeed be held accountable? Al-Suddi said, We will be held accountable. He said, Then the unbeliever went off and left him. He said, "When the believer saw him and did not look back, he returned and left him. The believer lives in hardship during a time and the unbeliever lives in ease." He said, "So when the Day of Resurrection comes and God admits the believer into Paradise, he passes by and sees land, palm trees, fruits, and rivers. He says, 'To whom does this belong?' It is said, 'This belongs to you.' He says, 'Glory be to God, or has the bounty of my deeds reached such a degree that I should be rewarded with the like of this?'" He said, "Then he passes by and sees slaves whose number cannot be counted. He says, 'To whom does this belong?' It is said, 'These belong to you.' He says, 'Glory be to God, or has the bounty of my deeds reached such a degree that I should be rewarded with the like of this.'" He said, "Then he passes by and sees a dome of red ruby, hollowed out in it, with a beautiful, beautiful woman in her eyes. He says, 'To whom does this belong?' It is said, 'This belongs to you.' He says, 'Glory be to God, or has the bounty of my deeds reached such a degree that I should be rewarded with the like of this.'" He said, "Then the believer remembers his unbelieving partner and says, 'Indeed, I had a companion.' He says, 'Would you To those who believe, When we die and become dust and bones, shall we then be recompensed? He said, Paradise is high and Hell is deep. Then God Almighty will show him his partner in the middle of Hell from among the people of Hell. When the believer sees him, he will recognize him and say, “By God, you were almost sent back. And had it not been for the grace of my Lord, you would have been among those brought forth. So are we not to die? Except our first death, and we are not to be punished. Indeed, this is the great attainment. For such things let the workers work.” He said: The believer remembers the hardships he went through in this world, and he does not remember anything that was more difficult for him than death.
37:62: God Almighty says: Is this that He mentioned of the delights of Paradise and what is in it of food, drink, marriage and other pleasures the best hospitality and gift? Or the tree of Zaqqum, meaning the one in Hell. It may be possible that what is meant by this is a specific tree, as some of them said that it is a tree whose branches extend to all the places of Hell, just as the Tree of Tuba has no house in Paradise except that it has a branch of it. It may be possible that what is meant by this is a type of tree called Zaqqum, as in His Almighty’s saying: And a tree that emerges from Mount Sinai, which produces oil and a condiment for those who eat, meaning the olive tree. This is supported by His Almighty’s saying: Then indeed, you, O astray deniers, * will eat from the tree of Zaqqum, and His Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers. Qatadah said: The tree of Zaqqum was mentioned, so the people of misguidance were tempted by it and they said: Your companion informs you that there is a tree in Hell, and fire eats trees. So God Almighty revealed: Indeed, it is a tree that emerges at the bottom of Hellfire. It was nourished. From the fire and from it it was created. Mujahid said, Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers. Abu Jahl, may God curse him, said, "Zaqqum is only dates and butter. You swallow it." I said, "The meaning of the verse is that We have only informed you, O Muhammad, about the tree of Zaqqum as a test by which We test people to see who among them will tell the truth and who will lie, as God, the Most High, says, "And We have not made the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people and [also] the accursed tree in the Qur'an. And We frighten them, but it only increases them in great transgression. And God, the Most High, says, Indeed, it is a tree that emerges at the bottom of Hellfire," meaning the bottom of its roots in the depths of the Fire. "Its fruit is like the heads of devils," to make it ugly and abhorrent to mention. Wahb ibn Munabbih said, "The hair of devils is directed toward the sky. He only likened it to the heads of devils, even though it is not known to those addressed, because it has been established in people's minds that devils are ugly to look at. It was also said that what is meant by that is a type of snake with hideous heads, or a type of plant whose fruit is extremely obscene. Both of these possibilities are debatable. Ibn Jarir mentioned them, but the first is stronger and more appropriate. And God knows best." God the Almighty said: "Then they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it." God the Almighty mentioned that they will eat from this tree, the appearance of which is the most hideous and ugly, despite its bad taste, smell and nature. They will be forced to eat from it because they will not find anything else but it and similar things, as God the Almighty said: "They will have no food except from the thorny plant, which neither nourishes nor avails against hunger." Ibn Abi Hatim may God have mercy on him said: My father told us, Amr ibn Marzuq told us, Shu'bah told us, from Al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited this verse and said: "Fear God as He should be feared. If a drop of Zaqqum were to fall into the oceans of this world, it would ruin the livelihood of the people of the earth, so how about those whose food it is?" Narrated by Al-Tirmidhi, Al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah from the hadith of Shu'bah. Al-Tirmidhi said: It is hasan saheeh. And the Almighty said: Then for them there will be a mixture of scalding water. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It means drinking scalding water on Zaqqum. And in a narration from him, he said: A mixture of scalding water, a mixture of scalding water. And another said: The scalding water will be mixed for them with pus and filth from what flows from their private parts and eyes. And Ibn Abi Hatim told us, my father told us, Haywah ibn Shuraih al-Hadrami told us, Baqiyah ibn al-Walid told us, on the authority of Safwan ibn Amr, and Ubaydullah ibn Busr told me, on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Bahili, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to say: “Water will be brought near to the people of Hell and they will hate it. When it is brought near, its face will be burned and the scalp will fall into it. When it drinks it, its intestines will be cut until they come out of its anus.” And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Amr ibn Rafi’ told us, Ya’qub ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of Ja’far and Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: When the people of Hell are hungry, they will seek help from the tree of Zaqqum and eat from it, and the skin of their faces will peel off. So if a passerby were to pass by them He knows them by their faces in it. Then thirst is poured upon them, and they cry out for help, and they are helped with water like molten brass, whose heat has reached its peak. When they bring it close to their mouths, the flesh of their faces, from which the skins have fallen, is scorched by its heat, and what is in their bellies melts, and they walk with their intestines flowing and their skins falling off. Then they are beaten with iron clubs, and every limb falls down on its own, calling for destruction. And the Almighty said: Then their return will surely be to Hellfire. That is, after this separation, their return will be to a blazing Fire, a blazing Hellfire, and a blazing Blaze. Sometimes in this place and sometimes in that, as the Almighty said: They will circulate between it and scalding water. This is how Qatada recited this verse, and it is a good and strong interpretation. Al-Suddi said regarding the recitation of Abdullah may God be pleased with him: Then their return will surely be to Hellfire. Abdullah may God be pleased with him used to say: “By the One in Whose Hand is my soul, the day will not reach midday on the Day of Resurrection until the people of Paradise have taken their rest in Paradise and the people of Hellfire have taken their rest in Hellfire.” Then he recited: The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be best in settlement and best in rest. Al-Thawri narrated from Maysarah from Al-Minhal bin Amr from Abu Ubaidah from Abdullah may God be pleased with him who said: The day will not reach midday on the Day of Resurrection until these people have taken their rest and those have taken their rest. Sufyan said: I think so. Then he recited: The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be best in settlement and best in rest. Then their rest will be to Hellfire. I said: According to this interpretation, then is a conjunction of one predicate to another. And the Almighty’s saying: Indeed, they found their fathers astray means that We only punished them with that because they found their fathers astray and followed them in it simply because of that without evidence or proof. That is why He said: And they hasten in their footsteps. Mujahid said that it is similar to running, and Saeed bin Jubayr said that it is foolish.

Sufyan said: I think so. Then he recited: The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be best in settlement and best in rest. Then their rest will be to Hellfire. I said: According to this interpretation, then is a conjunction of one predicate to another. That is why He said: And they hasten in their footsteps. Mujahid said that it is similar to running, and Saeed bin Jubayr said that it is foolish.
37:70: God Almighty says: Is this that He mentioned of the delights of Paradise and what is in it of food, drink, marriage and other pleasures the best hospitality and gift? Or the tree of Zaqqum, meaning the one in Hell. It may be possible that what is meant by this is a specific tree, as some of them said that it is a tree whose branches extend to all the places of Hell, just as the Tree of Tuba has no house in Paradise except that it has a branch of it. It may be possible that what is meant by this is a type of tree called Zaqqum, as in His Almighty’s saying: And a tree that emerges from Mount Sinai, which produces oil and a condiment for those who eat, meaning the olive tree. This is supported by His Almighty’s saying: Then indeed, you, O astray deniers, * will eat from the tree of Zaqqum, and His Almighty’s saying: Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers. Qatadah said: The tree of Zaqqum was mentioned, so the people of misguidance were tempted by it and they said: Your companion informs you that there is a tree in Hell, and fire eats trees. So God Almighty revealed: Indeed, it is a tree that emerges at the bottom of Hellfire. It was nourished. From the fire and from it it was created. Mujahid said, Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers. Abu Jahl, may God curse him, said, "Zaqqum is only dates and butter. You swallow it." I said, "The meaning of the verse is that We have only informed you, O Muhammad, about the tree of Zaqqum as a test by which We test people to see who among them will tell the truth and who will lie, as God, the Most High, says, "And We have not made the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people and [also] the accursed tree in the Qur'an. And We frighten them, but it only increases them in great transgression. And God, the Most High, says, Indeed, it is a tree that emerges at the bottom of Hellfire," meaning the bottom of its roots in the depths of the Fire. "Its fruit is like the heads of devils," to make it ugly and abhorrent to mention. Wahb ibn Munabbih said, "The hair of devils is directed toward the sky. He only likened it to the heads of devils, even though it is not known to those addressed, because it has been established in people's minds that devils are ugly to look at. It was also said that what is meant by that is a type of snake with hideous heads, or a type of plant whose fruit is extremely obscene. Both of these possibilities are debatable. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: It means drinking scalding water on Zaqqum. And in a narration from him, he said: A mixture of scalding water, a mixture of scalding water. And another said: The scalding water will be mixed for them with pus and filth from what flows from their private parts and eyes. And Ibn Abi Hatim told us, my father told us, Haywah ibn Shuraih al-Hadrami told us, Baqiyah ibn al-Walid told us, on the authority of Safwan ibn Amr, and Ubaydullah ibn Busr told me, on the authority of Abu Umamah al-Bahili, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he used to say: “Water will be brought near to the people of Hell and they will hate it. When it is brought near, its face will be burned and the scalp will fall into it. When it drinks it, its intestines will be cut until they come out of its anus.” And Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Amr ibn Rafi’ told us, Ya’qub ibn Abdullah told us, on the authority of Ja’far and Harun ibn Antara, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, who said: When the people of Hell are hungry, they will seek help from the tree of Zaqqum and eat from it, and the skin of their faces will peel off. So if a passerby were to pass by them He knows them by their faces in it. Then thirst is poured upon them, and they cry out for help, and they are helped with water like molten brass, whose heat has reached its peak. When they bring it close to their mouths, the flesh of their faces, from which the skins have fallen, is scorched by its heat, and what is in their bellies melts, and they walk with their intestines flowing and their skins falling off. 37:71: God Almighty tells us about the past nations that most of them were astray and used to associate other gods with God. God Almighty mentioned that He sent among them warners who warned of God’s wrath and warned them of His power and punishment against those who disbelieved in Him and worshipped other than Him. They persisted in disobeying and denying His messengers, so He destroyed and annihilated the disbelievers and saved the believers, granted them victory and made them triumphant. For this reason God Almighty said: Then see how was the end of those who were warned, except for the chosen servants of God.

37:75: When God the Almighty mentioned that most of the ancients had strayed from the path of salvation, He began to explain that in detail. He mentioned Noah, peace be upon him, and what he encountered from his people of denial, and that only a few of them believed despite the long period of time he lived among them for a thousand years minus fifty years. When that became long and their denial became intense, and whenever he called upon them they became more averse, he called upon his Lord, Indeed, I am defeated, so grant me victory. So God the Almighty became angry with them, and for this reason the Almighty said: And Noah called upon Us, and excellent are the respondent. That is, excellent are the respondent to him. And We saved him and his family from the great distress, which is the denial and harm. And We made his descendants the survivors. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, saying: Only the descendants of Noah, peace be upon him, remained. Sa`id ibn Abi `Aruba said on the authority of Qatada regarding the words of God Almighty: And We made his descendants the survivors, he said: All people are from the descendants of Noah, peace be upon him. At-Tirmidhi, Ibn Jarir, and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from the hadith of Sa`id ibn Bashir on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Samurah, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, regarding the words of God Almighty: And We made his descendants the survivors, he said: Sam, Ham, and Japheth. Imam Ahmad said: Abdul Wahhab told us on the authority of Sa`id on the authority of Qatada on the authority of Al-Hasan on the authority of Samurah, may God be pleased with him, that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Sam is the father of the Arabs, Ham is the father of the Abyssinians, and Japheth is the father of the Romans. At-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Bishr ibn Mu`adh Al-`Aqdi on the authority of Yazid ibn Zari` on the authority of Sa`id, who is Ibn Abi `Aruba, on the authority of Qatada with it. Al-Hafiz Abu `Umar ibn `Abd Al-Barr said: It was narrated on the authority of `Imran ibn Husayn, may God be pleased with him, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, something similar. What is meant by the Romans here are the first Romans, and they are the Greeks who are descended from Rumi ibn Lati ibn Yunan ibn Japheth, son of Noah, peace be upon him. Then it was narrated from the hadith of Ismail bin Ayyash, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, on the authority of Saeed bin Al-Musayyab, who said: Noah, peace be upon him, had three children: Shem, Japheth, and Ham. Each of these three had children. Shem gave birth to the Arabs, Persians, and Romans, and Japheth gave birth to the Turks, Slavs, Gog and Magog, and Ham gave birth to the Copts, Sudanese, and Berbers. Something similar to this was narrated from Wahb bin Munabbih, and God knows best. And the words of God Almighty: And We left for him among later generations Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, said: He is mentioned with goodness. Mujahid said: It means a tongue of truth for all the prophets. Qatada and As-Suddi said: May God preserve for him good praise among later generations. Ad-Dahhak said: Peace and good praise. The Almighty’s saying: “Peace be upon Noah among the worlds” explains why He preserved the beautiful remembrance and good praise for him, that he is greeted in all groups and nations. Thus do We reward the doers of good, meaning, this is how We reward whoever among the servants does good in obeying God Almighty, and We make for him a tongue of truth by which he is remembered after him according to his rank in that. Then the Almighty said: Indeed, he was of Our believing servants, meaning, the ones who believed, believed in God, and were certain. Then We drowned the others, meaning, We destroyed them, so that not a single eye of them remained, nor a memory, nor an eye, nor a trace, and they are not known except by this ugly description.

37:88: Abraham, peace be upon him, said that to his people so that he would stay in the city when they went to their festival, because the time had come for them to go out to their festival, so he wanted to be alone with their gods to break them, so he said to them words that were true in reality, and they understood from them that he was sick according to what they believed, so they turned away from him in retreat. Qatada said: The Arabs say to someone who thinks, He looked at the stars. Qatada meant that he looked at the sky thinking about what would distract them, and he said, I am sick, meaning weak. As for the hadith that Ibn Jarir narrated here, Abu Kurayb told us, Abu Usamah told us, Hisham told me, on the authority of Muhammad, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that the Messenger of God, peace be upon him, said: “Ibrahim, peace be upon him, did not lie except three lies: two for the sake of God Almighty, his saying, ‘I am sick,’ and his saying, ‘Rather, their leader did it,’ and his saying about Sarah, she is my sister.” It is a hadith that is narrated in the Sahihs and Sunans through various chains of narration, but this is not from Chapter: The true lie whose doer is blameworthy, God forbid, and no, and why. The term lying is used in this way metaphorically, but it is an euphemism in speech for a legitimate religious purpose, as came in the hadith, Indeed, in euphemisms there is an escape from lying. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Umar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud’an, on the authority of Abu Nadrah, on the authority of Abu Sa’id may God be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said regarding the three words of Abraham (blessings and peace of God be upon him), in which he said, Not one of them was a word except that it led to a breach of the religion of God the Most High, “Then he said, ‘Indeed, I am ill.’” He said, Rather, this, their leader, has done it, and he said to the king when he wanted to take his wife, She is my sister. Sufyan said regarding his statement, Indeed, I am ill, meaning stricken with plague. They would flee from one who had been stricken with plague, so he wanted to be alone with their gods. Al-Awfi said the same from Ibn Abbas may God be pleased with them both, regarding the statement of God the Most High: Then he looked at the stars and said, ‘Indeed, I am ill.’ While he was in the house of their gods, they said to him, Go out. He said, Indeed, I have been stricken with plague. So they left him for fear of the plague. Qatada said that Saeed bin Al-Musayyab saw a star rise and said, I am ill. The Prophet of God struggled with his religion. He said, ‘I am ill.’ Others said, He said, ‘I am ill.’ In reference to what was coming, meaning the illness of death. It was also said that he meant, I am ill, meaning sick of heart from your worship of idols other than God Almighty. Al-Hasan Al-Basri said: The people of Abraham went out to their festival and they wanted him to go out, so he lay on his back and said, I am ill, and he began to look at the sky. When they went out, he went to their idols and broke them. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it. For this reason, God Almighty said, So they turned away from him in flight, meaning he went to them after they had gone out quickly and hidden. He said, ‘Will you not eat?’ This is because they had placed food before them as an offering so that they would be blessed in it. Al-Suddi said: “Abraham, peace be upon him, entered the house of the gods and behold, they were in a great hall. Facing the door of the hall was a great idol, next to it were smaller ones, one next to the other, each idol smaller than it, until they reached the door of the hall. They had prepared food and placed it in front of the gods and said, ‘When we return, and the gods have blessed our food, we will eat it.’ When Abraham, peace be upon him, looked at the food in front of them, he said, ‘Will you not eat? What is the matter with you that you do not speak?’” And the Almighty’s statement, Then he struck them with his right hand, Al-Farra’ said, means that he struck them with his right hand. Qatadah and Al-Jawhari said, Then he attacked them with his right hand. He struck them with his right hand because it is more severe and more painful. For this reason, he left them scattered except for one of their largest ones, so that perhaps they might return to it, as the explanation of that was mentioned in Surat Al-Anbiya’, peace be upon them. And the Almighty’s saying here: So they came to him in haste. Mujahid and others said that it means they hastened. This story here is brief, but in Surat Al-Anbiya it is explained in detail, for when they returned, they did not know at first who had done that until they discovered and inquired, and they knew that it was Abraham, peace be upon him, who had done that. When they came to rebuke him, he began to rebuke and criticize them, saying, Do you worship what you carve? That is, do you worship idols other than God, what you carve and make with your own hands? And God created you and what you do? It is possible that what is a source, so the meaning of the statement would be He created you and your work. It is possible that it means who, and its meaning is And God created you and what you do. Both statements are related, and the first is more evident because of what Al-Bukhari narrated in the Book of the Actions of the Servants on the authority of Ali bin Al-Madini on the authority of Marwan bin Muawiyah on the authority of Abu Malik on the authority of Rib’i bin Harash on the authority of Hudhayfah, may God be pleased with him, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, who said, God Almighty creates every maker and his craft. Some of them read, And God created you and what you do. Then, when the proof was established against them, they turned to seizing him by hand and by force, so they said, Build for him a structure and throw him into Hellfire. And what happened to them was what was explained previously in Surat Al-Anbiya, peace and blessings be upon them. God saved him from the Fire, made him victorious over them, raised his proof and supported it. For this reason, God Almighty said, So they wanted to… "We plotted against them, but We made them the lowest."

37:99: God Almighty says, informing about His friend Abraham, peace be upon him, that after God Almighty granted him victory over his people and he despaired of their faith after they had witnessed the great signs, he emigrated from among them and said, “Indeed, I am going to my Lord, He will guide me. My Lord, grant me from among the righteous.” Meaning obedient children in place of his people and clan whom he had left. God Almighty said, So We gave him good tidings of a forbearing boy. This boy is Ishmael, peace be upon him, for he was the first son that Abraham, peace be upon him, was given good tidings of, and he is older than Isaac, according to the agreement of the Muslims and People of the Book. Rather, in the text of their Book, Ishmael, peace be upon him, was born when Abraham, peace be upon him, was eighty-six years old, and Isaac was born when Abraham, peace be upon him, was ninety-nine years old. They believe that God Almighty commanded Abraham to slaughter his only son, and in another version, his firstborn. So they falsely and slanderously inserted Isaac here, and this is not permissible because it contradicts the text of His Book. Rather, they inserted… Isaac because he was their father and Ishmael was the father of the Arabs, so they envied them and increased that and distorted the word your only son to mean the one you have no one else with you, because Ishmael had gone with him and his mother to Mecca, which is a false interpretation and distortion, because your only son is only said to someone who has no one else. Also, the first born to him has a status that no other son after him has, so the command to slaughter him is more eloquent in trial and test. A group of scholars have said that the one to be slaughtered was Isaac, and this was reported from a group of the Salaf, and it was even transmitted from some of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, as well. This is not in the Book or the Sunnah, and I do not think that it was received except from the rabbis of the People of the Book, and a Muslim took it without proof. The Book of God is a witness and guide to the fact that it was Ishmael, because it mentioned the good report of a forbearing boy and mentioned that he was the one to be slaughtered, then it said after that, And We gave him good tidings of Isaac, a prophet among the righteous. And when the angels gave Abraham good tidings of Isaac, they said, Indeed, We give you good tidings of a knowledgeable boy. And God Almighty said, So We gave her good tidings of Isaac, and after Isaac, Jacob. That is, a son was born to him during their lifetime called Jacob, and he would be from his descendants. After that, he was ordered to slaughter him while he was young, because God Almighty promised them that he would have children and offspring. So how can he be ordered to slaughter him while he was young, and Ishmael was described here as the forbearing one because it is appropriate for this situation? And the Almighty’s saying: And when he reached with him the age of striving means he grew up and became mature and began to go with his father and walk with him. Abraham, peace be upon him, used to go all the time to check on his son and his son’s mother in the land of Paran and look into their situation. It was mentioned that he used to ride quickly on Buraq to there, and God knows best. And on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, and Mujahid, Ikrimah, Saeed bin Jubayr, Ata’ al-Khurasani, Zaid bin Aslam, and others: And when he reached with him the age of striving means he grew up and was able to do what his father did of striving and working. And when he reached with him the age of striving, he said, ‘O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I am slaughtering you, so see what you think.’ Ubayd bin Umair said: The vision of the prophets is revelation. Then he recited this verse: He said, ‘O my son, indeed I have seen in a dream that I am slaughtering you, so see what you think.’ Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali bin Al-Hussein bin Al-Junayd told us, Abu Abdul Malik Al-Karandi told us, Sufyan bin Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Isra’il bin Yunus, on the authority of Samak, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: The visions of the prophets in a dream are revelation.
